after: its payload carries a `reason` drawn from a closed set (`act-threw` and `workspace-commit-unknown` at v0.1) and, when present, an `exit_code` of `null`. `workspace-commit-unknown` is the local counterpart of `act-threw`: a transaction over several files in one workspace was applied and the workspace then read back as neither the approved before-state nor the approved after-state, which POSIX permits because it offers no atomic multi-file rename. The two are separate members rather than one, because a reader deciding what to do next needs to know whether the unknown effect was a remote call or a half-written local tree, and the recoveries have nothing in common. An implementation writing this reason MUST retain, outside the log, a durable record naming the before-state and the after-state it was moving between, and MUST NOT resolve the outcome from it: recovery reports which of the two states it can prove and leaves anything else to `execution.reconciled`. (Amended APRV-325.2, pending sign-off.)
before: its payload carries a `reason` drawn from a closed set (`act-threw` at v0.1) and, when present, an `exit_code` of `null`.
